title: Transplantation of Induced Pluripotent Stem Cell-derived Mesoangioblast-like Myogenic Progenitors in Mouse Models of Muscle Regeneration
protocol: Generate a stable cell line of IDEMs transduced with the tamoxifen-inducible MyoD-ER lentiviral vector, titrating the multiplicity of infection (MOI).
Coat a 3.5 cm dish with 1 ml of 1% Matrigel.
Incubate the coated dish for 30 min at 37 °C.
Wash the plate twice with medium.
Seed 1 x 10^5 MyoD-ER transduced IDEMs in the 3.5 cm tissue culture dish.
Incubate the seeded cells at 37 °C in growth medium until confluence is reached.
Add 1 μM 4OH-tamoxifen into the growth medium (1st dose) after reaching confluence.
Replace the growth medium with differentiation medium supplemented with 1 μM 4OH-tamoxifen (2nd and last dose) after 24 hr.
Replace half of the medium with fresh differentiation medium every other day.
Examine daily for myotube formation in cultures.
After one week, wash the plates gently with PBS.
Fix the plates with 4 % paraformaldehyde for 5 min at RT.
Perform an immunofluorescence staining with antibodies against myosin heavy chain (MyHC).
Counterstain with a nuclear dye (e.g., Hoechst).
Pretreat the animals with an intra-peritoneal injection of 3.5 μl/g of 10 mg/ml tamoxifen (liposoluble form) 24 hr before transplantation.
Pretreat cells adding 1 μM 4OH-tamoxifen (aqueous form) into the growth medium overnight before the transplantation day.
Administer anesthesia and analgesia to the mouse following specific guidelines.
Inject 25 μl of 100 μM cardiotoxin (CTX; from Naja mossambica mossambica) in the tibialis anterior (TA) muscles.
Detach the cells by trypsinization and count 24 hr after treating the animals with tamoxifen and CTX.
Centrifuge the cells at 232 x g for 5 min.
Wash the cell pellet in Ca2+- and Mg2+-free PBS.
Centrifuge the washed cell pellet.
Gently resuspend the cell pellet in Ca2+- and Mg2+-free PBS to achieve a final concentration of 10^6 cells/30 μl.
Inject 30 μl of cell suspension into previously injured muscles using a syringe with a 29 or 30 G needle.
Remove the needle slowly from the muscle, avoiding spillage through the needle's track.
Transplant the contralateral TA by injecting 30 μl of Ca2+- and Mg2+-free PBS as a control.
Treat animals with tamoxifen for six additional days.
Administer analgesia (e.g., Carprofen) for two additional days.
Explant muscles from 14 days after transplantation onwards.
Process and analyze the samples as detailed in Protocols 4 and 5.
Pretreat animals with an intra-peritoneal injection of 3.5 μl/g of 10 mg/ml tamoxifen (liposoluble formulation) 24 hours before transplantation.
Add 1 μM 4OH-tamoxifen (aqueous formulation) to the growth medium overnight before the transplantation day.
Detach cells by trypsinization.
Count detached cells.
Centrifuge cells at 232 x g for 5 minutes.
Wash cell pellet in Ca²⁺- and Mg²⁺-free PBS.
Centrifuge washed cell pellet.
Resuspend pellet in Ca²⁺- and Mg²⁺-free PBS to a concentration of 10⁶ cells/30 μl.
Administer analgesia and disinfect the skin of the animal with a povidone iodine- or chlorexidine-based disinfectant.
Localize the tibialis anterior (TA), gastrocnemius (GC), and quadriceps femoris (QC) muscles.
Insert 5 mm of a 29 or 30 G needle into the TA muscle, 2 mm below the insertion of the proximal tendon in a craniocaudal direction with a 15° inclination relative to the tibia.
Slowly inject 30 μl of cell suspension while retracting the needle, ensuring that the syringe is empty only when 2 mm of the needle remains inside the muscle.

For the GC and QC muscles, insert the needle 2 mm above the myotendinous junction of the Achilles tendon for the GC and 2 mm above the distal tendon for the QC in a caudocranial direction with a 15° inclination relative to the femur.
Carefully remove the needle from the muscle while avoiding spillage of the cell suspension through the needle's track.
Pretreat animals and cells as described above in step 2.1.1.
Detach cells by trypsinization.
Filter the cell suspension with a 40 μm cell strainer.
Count and centrifuge the cells at 232 x g for 5 min.
Wash the cell pellet in Ca²⁺- and Mg²⁺-free PBS.
Centrifuge and then resuspend the pellet in Ca²⁺- and Mg²⁺-free PBS with 0.2 International Units of sodium heparin to a final concentration of 10⁶ cells/50 μl (optional).
Add 10% Patent blue dye to the solution to achieve a final concentration of 1.25 mg/ml.
Administer anesthesia and analgesia to the mouse according to institutional guidelines.
Shave the inguinal region.
Disinfect the skin with povidone iodine- or chlorhexidine-based disinfectant.
Make a 5-7 mm incision in the inguinal region.
Localize the femoral bundle including vein, artery, and nerve.
Gently remove the connective fascia that covers the bundle with forceps.
Separate the femoral vein and nerve from the artery by gently introducing the tip of a forceps in between them.
Enlargen the hole progressively to separate the structures.
Lift the artery with one tip of the forceps.
Clamp the artery with the other tip.
Puncture the artery with a syringe equipped with a 30 G needle.
Inject 50 μl of cell suspension downstream of the clamped area at an infusion speed of approximately 5 μl/sec.
Carefully resuspend the cells in the syringe before injection to avoid precipitation and air bubble formation.
Monitor for patent blue dye uptake to confirm correct injection.
Slowly remove the needle from the artery to restore bloodstream in the limb.
Apply pressure with sterile gauze to stop bleeding as required.
Cauterize if necessary to control hemorrhage.
Suture the wound after confirming no further bleeding.
Monitor animals until recovery from anesthesia.
Administer analgesia for 3 days.
Inspect the wound daily.
Discuss with animal facility personnel if wound infection is observed.
Administer antibiotics as required.
Begin treadmill test two weeks after cell transplantation.
Set treadmill at a speed of 6 m/min for 10 min to acclimatize animals.
Repeat acclimatization procedure every other day for one week.
Record all measurements at the same hour daily to avoid circadian cycle biases.
Place the animals into the treadmill inclined at 10°.
Turn on the treadmill with a starting speed of 6 m/min.
Increase the speed by 2 m/min every 2 min.
Gently touch an animal lying in the resting area for more than 5 sec to stimulate reengagement.
Record the performance (time and distance) of each animal.
Repeat measurements weekly or every 10 days for at least 3 times.
Repeat the same procedure after transplantation.
Analyze performance data by comparing it to baseline values.
Plot values as a percentage of average motor capacity relative to baseline.
Conduct analysis using one- or two-way ANOVA test followed by appropriate post-test.
Harvest transplanted and control muscles at appropriate time points.
Assess engraftment by direct fluorescence under UV-equipped stereomicroscope if cells are labeled with GFP.
Lay freshly isolated muscles vertically in tragacanth gum (6% w/v).
Dehydrate samples in prechilled isopentane for one minute.
Freeze samples in liquid nitrogen for at least 2 minutes.
Store frozen samples at -80 °C.
Obtain 7 μm thick sections on polarized slides using a cryostat.
Collect approximately 30-40 sections per slide, sampling the majority of the muscle.
Prepare series of sections into a 1.5 ml tube for molecular biology/biochemistry assays.
Evaluate cell engraftment with immunofluorescent staining appropriate to experimental setup.
Stain sections with antibody against Lamin A/C to detect grafted human cell nuclei.
Visualize overall structure of the muscle using an antibody against Laminin.
Detect donor-derived restoration of Sgca protein absent in dystrophic animal.
Quantify, using a fluorescence microscope, the number of donor nuclei per muscle section inside and outside muscle fibers.
Quantify, using a fluorescence microscope, the number of donor-derived skeletal myofibers per section.
Fix freshly isolated muscles with 4% paraformaldehyde for 1 hr at 4 °C.
Dehydrate samples with an ascending sucrose gradient (e.g., 7.5-15-30% w/v).
Leave samples overnight in the highest sucrose solution.
Embed samples in Tissue Tek OCT.
Place embedded samples in prechilled isopentane until OCT becomes solid, avoiding complete immersion of samples.
Freeze samples in liquid nitrogen for at least 2 min.
Store frozen samples immediately at -80 °C.
Obtain 7 μm thick sections with a cryostat.
Stain sections with hematoxylin and eosin according to standard manufacturer's protocols.
Stain sections with Masson's trichrome according to standard manufacturer's protocols.
